'''Ivette Fuentes''' (born 7 October 1972) is a Professor of [[Quantum Physics]] at the [[University of Southampton]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Professor Ivette Fuentes Guridi {{!}} Physics and Astronomy {{!}} University of Southampton|url=https://www.phys.soton.ac.uk/people/ifg1n20|access-date=2022-01-20|website=www.phys.soton.ac.uk}}</ref> and Emmy Fellow (Fellow by Special Election) at [[Keble College]], [[University of Oxford]]. Her work considers fundamental [[quantum mechanics]], [[quantum optics]] and their interplay with [[general relativity]]. She is interested in how quantum information theory can make use of relativistic effects.

== Early life and education ==
Fuentes was born and raised in [[Mexico]]. Whilst she was at high school she was interested in dance and considered becoming a professional ballet dancer.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://medium.com/@ja.alper20/a-conversation-with-quantum-physicist-ivette-fuentes-192db691c96b|title=A Conversation with Quantum Physicist Ivette Fuentes|last=Alper|first=Jerry|date=2018-02-21|website=Medium|language=en|access-date=2019-11-21}}</ref> Fuentes studied physics at the [[National Autonomous University of Mexico]] and graduated in 1997.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.perimeterinstitute.ca/people/ivette-fuentes|title=Ivette Fuentes {{!}} Perimeter Institute|website=www.perimeterinstitute.ca|access-date=2019-11-21}}</ref> She worked with [[Deborah Dultzin]] on [[Seyfert galaxy|Seyfert galaxies]]. Whilst at UNAM Fuentes won a competition to spend a summer at [[Fermilab]] and she decided that she wanted to continue working in physics. Fuentes earned her doctoral degree at [[Imperial College London]] in 2003 under the supervision of [[Peter Knight (physicist)|Peter Knight]] and [[Vlatko Vedral]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=147278|title=Ivette Fuentes - The Mathematics Genealogy Project|website=www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu|access-date=2019-11-21}}</ref> She moved to the [[Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics]] as a postdoctoral fellow, where she worked until 2006. In 2004 she was selected as a [[University of Oxford]] Junior Research Fellow and joined [[Mansfield College, Oxford]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://medienportal.univie.ac.at/uniview/professuren/cv/artikel/univ-prof-ivette-fuentes-guridi-phd/|title=Univ.-Prof. Ivette Fuentes Guridi, PhD|website=medienportal.univie.ac.at|language=de|access-date=2019-11-21}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.science.org/content/article/outracing-quantum-weirdness|title=Outracing Quantum Weirdness|last1=Cho|first1=Adrian|date=2005-09-13|website=Science {{!}} AAAS|language=en|access-date=2019-11-21}}</ref> She was appointed an [[Alexander von Humboldt]] fellowship to join [[Technische Universität Berlin]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://lifeboat.com/ex/bios.ivette.fuentes|title=Lifeboat Foundation Bios: Dr. Ivette Fuentes|website=lifeboat.com|access-date=2019-11-21}}</ref>

== Research and career ==
Fuentes is working on new ways to store and use information using quantum systems. She looks to use [[relativistic quantum mechanics]] to improve information tasks such as [[quantum cryptography]] and [[quantum teleportation]]. She demonstrated a quantum thermometer that could measure the temperature of [[Bose–Einstein condensate]]s.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/mg21829194-600-quantum-thermometer-could-measure-coldest-thing-ever/|title=Quantum thermometer could measure coldest thing ever|last=Aron|first=Jacob|website=www.newscientist.com|access-date=2019-11-21}}</ref> Fuentes was awarded an [[Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council]] Career Acceleration Fellowship and joined the [[University of Nottingham]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.quantum.physik.uni-potsdam.de/members/ivetteschuller.html|title=Quantum Optics Group at the University of Potsdam|website=www.quantum.physik.uni-potsdam.de|access-date=2019-11-21|archive-date=2021-06-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210627040424/http://www.quantum.physik.uni-potsdam.de/members/ivetteschuller.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 2015 Fuentes joined the [[University of Vienna]] where she is a member of the theoretical quantum optics group.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://qt.eu/engage/community/directories/university-vienna-quantum-optics-quantum-nanophysics-and-quantum-information/|title=University Vienna - Quantum Optics, Quantum Nanophysics and Quantum Information|website=Quantum Technology|language=en-US|access-date=2019-11-21|archive-date=2020-09-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200908090041/https://qt.eu/engage/community/directories/university-vienna-quantum-optics-quantum-nanophysics-and-quantum-information/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.newscientist.com/video/2183450-ivette-fuentes-how-to-build-a-quantum-teleporter/|title=Quantum thermometer could measure coldest thing ever|last=Aron|first=Jacob|website=www.newscientist.com|access-date=2019-11-21}}</ref> She was awarded funding from the [[Foundational Questions Institute]] to study quantum theory.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://fqxi.org/grants/large/awardees/view/__details/2016/fuentes|title=FQXi - Foundational Questions Institute|website=fqxi.org|language=en-US|access-date=2019-11-21}}</ref> In 2017 Fuentes co-founded the Penrose Institute, an organisation that looks to test the scientific ideas of [[Roger Penrose]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://penroseinstitute.com/about/ivette-fuentes/|title=Ivette Fuentes|website=The Penrose Institute|language=en-US|access-date=2019-11-21}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.newswise.com/articles/the-roger-penrose-institute-a-collaboration-from-london-san-diego-tucson-formed-in-san-diego|title=Roger Penrose Institute to Form in San Diego|website=www.newswise.com|access-date=2019-11-21}}</ref> Unlike many researchers at Harvard and MIT, Fuentes rejected financial support from [[Jeffrey Epstein]], citing ethical reasons.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.science.org/content/article/what-kind-researcher-did-sex-offender-jeffrey-epstein-fund-he-told-science-he-died|title=What kind of researcher did sex offender Jeffrey Epstein like to fund? He told Science before he died|date=2019-09-19|website=Science {{!}} AAAS|language=en|access-date=2019-11-21}}</ref>

Fuentes has spoken at [[New Scientist]] Live, where she discussed building equipment for [[quantum teleportation]].<ref>{{Citation|title=Ivette Fuentes|url=https://www.facebook.com/newscilive/videos/ivette-fuentes/1933852376905194/|language=en|access-date=2019-11-21}}</ref> She has worked with the expressionist artist Benjamin Arizmendi on an art{{snd}}science project entitled "The Aesthetics of Entanglement".<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://ivettefuentes.weebly.com/art-and-quantum.html|title=Art and quantum|website=Ivette Fuentes|language=en|access-date=2019-11-21}}</ref>
